data.body:
[P2] Preserve emission identity across invocation boundaries

Every resume creates a new plugin and resets this counter, but SQS and DynamoDB use the same `executionArn` across invocations. If a burst advances the suspending invocation's timestamps ahead of wall time, a fast resume can reuse those milliseconds; a backward clock adjustment across invocations can also cause overlap. For example, a suspension record bumped to `.124Z` collides with a resumed instance's first record when its clock reads `.124Z`. SQS silently suppresses the resume record, and DynamoDB overwrites earlier history. Use a separate emission identity containing an invocation-unique token and sequence for these exporter keys, while retaining fixed-width timestamps. Add a regression covering two plugin instances for the same ARN with overlapping clock readings.
